llm.summary: This is a Git command helper, but it gives an agent broad activation wording and destructive repository commands without enough safety checks.

dimensions.detail: Exec access is proportionate for Git workflow guidance, but the examples include destructive commands and a predictable /tmp script path without requiring status checks, backups, clean worktrees, or explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a single Markdown skill with no bundled executable code; however, front matter lists allowed-tools as read and exec while a separate tools block includes write, creating unclear authority disclosure.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The description and trigger condition broaden activation to generic AI model, dialogue, agent orchestration, and LLM application scenarios instead of limiting use to explicit Git/version-control tasks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no artifact-backed persistence, background workers, credential harvesting, tool hijacking, remote payload retrieval, or privileged system changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main purpose is coherent with advanced Git workflows, but the skill includes high-impact commands such as interactive rebase, reset --hard, cherry-pick, and forced worktree removal that can rewrite history or discard local work.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your agent can execute commands. Only use it inside repositories you intend to modify, ask the agent to run git status and create a backup branch before destructive Git operations, and treat reset --hard, rebase history edits, and forced worktree removal as actions requiring explicit approval.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad AI/agent/LLM trigger language is not needed for a Git workflow skill and could cause the skill to activate outside repository tasks.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The artifact itself supports the mismatch: the body is a Git command cookbook, while the trigger language is much wider than Git operations.
[SQP-2] expected: Recovery guidance is within scope, but reset --hard and forced worktree removal are presented without clear warnings that local changes can be discarded.
[TM1] expected: The reset --hard examples are Git-domain commands, but they normalize destructive state changes without confirmation, backup branch guidance, or clean-worktree checks.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Generic API, HTTPS, CRUD, import/export, and output-format language appears templated and does not match the actual Markdown-only Git command behavior; I treated this as under-disclosure/confusion, not evidence of hidden network capability.
[T09] expected: Using a script with git bisect run is purpose-aligned, but the fixed /tmp/test-for-bug.sh path is an avoidable unsafe pattern on shared systems.
